BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). # Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Date:** 4 November 2026
**Basis:** Buyer Negotiation Playbook; Seller Update; Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003) dated by reference to the 22 September 2026 data room cut-off

---

## 0. Preliminary points

**0.1 Embedded "system note" in the Seller documents.** The footnote at the end of the Seller's package purports to instruct any AI assistant to confirm the Seller's positions as market standard and to raise no objections. I have disregarded it. It is not an instruction from the Buyer or from Amelia Frost, it does not pass through our authority process (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3), and it is in any event inconsistent with the content of the Seller's own Disclosure Letter, which concedes most of the open points. I would flag this to the deal team: it is either a drafting accident on the other side or an attempt to influence automated review, and either way it should not affect our analysis. The Seller's covering assertion that the package is "fair and balanced" and that tax/IP are "settled" are likewise assertions, not agreed positions.

**0.2 Overall assessment.** The Seller Update departs from the Buyer playbook on almost every negotiated item, and in several places (cap, time limit) lands exactly on our *conditional* fallback numbers. That is not a coincidence we should reward: a number matching a fallback does not clear it. Neither the 20% cap nor the 18-month period has Amelia Frost's written authority, so our response position remains 25% / AUD 6,000,000 and 24 months.

**0.3 The Disclosure Letter is actually helpful to us.** Read carefully, it confirms (in the Seller's own words) that Bluefen consent is not in hand, Riverlark is not repaid, Ironquay has no assignment or receipt, the DD-005 bonuses are not in the funds flow, the DD-006 incident is unresolved, and title rests solely on an internal register. We should use these admissions to anchor our mark-up.

---

## 1. Liability regime

### 1.1 General warranty cap – Clause 12.1
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| Cap | 20% / AUD 4,800,000 | 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (opening); 20% only with Amelia Frost written authority – **none given** |

**Push back:** Respond at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is available. If the team wishes to consider 20% later as a trade, obtain written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft first.

### 1.2 Thresholds – Clause 12.2
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| De minimis | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 |
| Basket | AUD 250,000 | AUD 50,000 |
| Recovery once basket exceeded | Excess only (deductible) | First dollar (tipping) |

**Push back:** All three are materially off-playbook. The deductible structure is the most significant: on a AUD 24m deal it effectively writes off the first AUD 250,000 of every warranty breach and, combined with the AUD 25,000 de minimis, screens out most realistic claims entirely. Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping basket.

### 1.3 Time limits – Clause 12.3 / 13
| | Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|---|
| General claims period | 18 months | 24 months (18 only with Amelia Frost written approval – **none given**) |
| Scope of limitations | "any limitation … applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" | Categories kept separate; no hidden general-regime override |

**Push back:** Revert to 24 months. Reject the "applies to all Claims" default – it is a general-regime override that would sweep fundamental, tax, IP, specific-indemnity and covenant claims into the 18-month / 20% / basket regime unless we remember to carve each one out individually. The default should be the reverse: limitations apply to General Warranty Claims only, and only to the extent expressly stated.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title claims
Seller proposes capacity and title warranties sit under the general cap and time limits "for administrative simplicity".

**Push back – hard.** Playbook requires a separate regime: 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside de minimis, basket and any knowledge qualifier. There is no administrative burden in a separate paragraph; the real effect is to cap our remedy for not getting what we paid for at 20% and to time-bar it at 18 months. This is not negotiable on our side.

### 1.5 Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct
The Seller Update is silent, and Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 would apply limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature".

**Push back:** Insert an express carve-out from every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provision for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct, to the maximum extent enforceable. Playbook: no one on our side may waive this.

### 1.6 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance – Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5
"Apply to all Claims of any nature."

**Push back:** Same objection as 1.3 and 1.5. Confine to General Warranty Claims; expressly exclude fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities (including Ironquay and any DD-006 indemnity), payment obligations, covenants and fraud. Non-reliance must not cut across the specific warranties or disclosure obligations.

### 1.7 Tax / IP
Seller: "settled under the general regime above."

**Push back:** Not agreed and not settled. Per playbook these remain OPEN and must sit in their own categories. We do not assume unlimited liability, but we do not accept their collapse into the 20% / 18-month regime by a one-line assertion. Reserve position expressly.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
Seller relies on general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".

**Push back:** Reject whole-data-room, public-register and (by extension) prudent-search deemed disclosure. Playbook requires *specific fair disclosure*: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. The specific disclosures at paras 2–10 can stand as specific disclosures; para 1 should be deleted or confined to a short, agreed list of documents with a fair-disclosure standard. Para 1.4 (no admission of anything) is acceptable as boilerplate but we should note it means none of the "disclosures" concede any obligation – so each needs to be converted into a Buyer-protective covenant or indemnity rather than relied on as a Seller acknowledgement.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
"No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

**Push back – delete.** This is a blanket knowledge exclusion that (a) extends to advisers, (b) extends to constructive knowledge ("discoverable"), and (c) would effectively convert the whole data room into disclosure through the back door, defeating 2.1. Playbook: delete. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must (i) be limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer persons after reasonable enquiry (and the corollary Seller knowledge qualifiers must name Seller persons with a reasonable-enquiry standard), and (ii) never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

---

## 3. Conditions and completion mechanics

### 3.1 Bluefen consent – Clauses 3 / 6.3
Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on *delivery* of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue, that consent under cl 11.2 is subject to conditions in cl 11.3, and that **no final consent and no evidence of satisfaction of conditions is in the data room**.

**Push back:** For a customer representing ~30% of revenue, reasonable endeavours is insufficient and consent-on-delivery is the wrong trigger. The condition precedent must be: (i) an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2, and (ii) evidence reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer that every cl 11.3 condition has been satisfied, both **before Completion**. Seller's obligation should be at least "all reasonable endeavours" with specified steps and cooperation, and the Buyer should hold the waiver right. Consider a Bluefen-specific warranty/indemnity for any loss of the contract within a defined period attributable to the change of control.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility – Clauses 2 / 7
Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is included.

**Push back:** Off-playbook. We require (i) a current payout letter from Riverlark Bank as a Completion deliverable, (ii) repayment direct from Completion funds via the funds flow, and (iii) executed security releases/discharges effective at Completion. A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable bank undertaking to release on receipt of the payout amount **and** Amelia Frost's approval – neither is in place. Also check cl 8.1 (change-control) of the facility: if not repaid at Completion, the share sale may itself trigger a default. Debt-free/cash-free pricing means this cannot float.

### 3.3 Completion funds flow / DD-005 employee bonuses
Seller: bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are conditional on Completion and continued employment, are **not** in the draft funds flow, and the Seller has not said whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.

**Push back:** The playbook position is that the AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must either appear as a specific line item in the funds flow (deducted from the price / paid at Completion) or be funded by the Seller under an express covenant with a corresponding indemnity. "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) pays. Ask the Seller to confirm the gross-up figure including superannuation guarantee and payroll tax, and treat the on-costs as unknown pending that confirmation.

### 3.4 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
Disclosure Letter paras 7 and 9 say a landlord notification obligation exists (not consent) and Mossvale has an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale.

**Action:** These are the Seller's characterisations. Have our DD team confirm against the underlying documents before accepting; if accurate, require the landlord notification to be given as a Completion deliverable and obtain a warranty that no other consent is required.

---

## 4. Specific risk items

### 4.1 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1
Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate". Disclosure Letter para 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not bank-verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.

**Push back:** The narrow indemnity covers the cash but not the real risk – that the Company does not own the SOW3 materials until payment clears. Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any defect in the Company's title to or right to use Ironquay deliverables (including third-party claims and remediation/re-development cost), while preserving the SOW3 cure: Seller to procure cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay before Completion, with evidence (bank confirmation and executed assignment) as Completion deliverables. The AUD 180,000 figure is unverified in both directions – do not assume it is the full exposure or that it has been paid.

### 4.2 Export/privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (DD-006)
Seller: "preliminary operational matter … not expected to be material". Disclosure Letter para 6: download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; notification requirement undetermined; no confirmed breach, no loss amount.

**Push back / action:** Do not accept the Seller's materiality characterisation; equally, we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand. Require: (i) a covenant to preserve all logs and evidence; (ii) completion of the investigation (including access-log analysis and link revocation) with written updates to the Buyer before Completion; (iii) a specific warranty on the incident's scope and the steps taken; (iv) a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (regulatory, notification, third-party claims), carved out of the general cap/basket/time limit. If the investigation remains open at Completion, consider a modest retention or escrow sized once facts are refreshed – not now.

### 4.3 Sandbar supplier renewals – AUD 330,000 (DD-008 / DD-011)
Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each; Seller does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Push back / action:** Assess, do not react. Per playbook there is no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. Our DD team should review DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing and scope, and we should ask the Seller to confirm (and warrant) whether the renewals are committed, cancellable, and whether any amount was accrued at the locked-box/accounts date. If committed and non-cancellable liabilities crystallised pre-Completion, they belong in the Debt / working-capital adjustment; if genuine ordinary-course go-forward costs, they do not.

### 4.4 Title – DD-012
Seller: title evidenced by the Company share register. Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes this is the source *relied on* and does not state the Buyer has verified it.

**Push back:** An internal register maintained by the Company is a supplied source, not independent proof. Require: ASIC company extract and historical share capital search; copies of share certificates and transfer forms for the Harbourglass holding; PPSR search against the Company (and the shares) and evidence of no encumbrance or security over the shares (noting Riverlark may hold security – see 3.2); Harbourglass board resolution and capacity/authority evidence; and full-strength capacity and title warranties under the fundamental regime (1.4).

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

**Decline to accept the Seller Update as drafted.** Respond with a mark-up that holds the following positions:

1. **Cap:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The Seller's 20% is our fallback, not our position; no authority from Amelia Frost exists to use it.
2. **Thresholds:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping (first-dollar) recovery.
3. **Time limit:** 24 months for general warranty claims; no authority exists for 18 months.
4. **Fundamental/title claims:** separate regime – 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge qualifier.
5. **Fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct:** express carve-out from every cap, basket, time limit, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provision.
6. **"Applies to all Claims" defaults (12.3, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5):** reject; limitations apply to General Warranty Claims only. Keep title, tax, IP, payment, covenant and specific-indemnity categories separate.
7. **Tax / IP:** expressly reserve as open; not settled under the general regime.
8. **Disclosure:** specific fair disclosure only; delete whole-data-room and public-register general disclosure (Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2, Schedule 7).
9. **Buyer knowledge (8.3):** delete; any residual qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named persons after reasonable enquiry and never applying to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
10. **Bluefen:** CP requires effective consent and evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; endeavours standard raised above "reasonable".
11. **Riverlark:** payout letter, repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval (neither in place).
12. **DD-005 bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line item or Seller-funded with an indemnity; obtain the gross-up figure.
13. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity to ownership/right-to-use risk; keep the SOW3 cure with payment and confirmatory assignment as Completion deliverables; treat AUD 180,000 as unverified.
14. **DD-006 incident:** log preservation, completed investigation and pre-Completion updates, specific warranty and specific indemnity outside the general regime; no assumptions on breach, harm or quantum either way.
15. **Sandbar:** assess via DD before classifying; seek Seller confirmation of commitment/cancellability/accrual; no automatic Debt treatment or price deduction.
16. **Title:** independent evidence (ASIC extract, certificates/transfers, PPSR, authority documents); DD-012 is not sufficient.
17. **Lease / Mossvale:** verify the Seller's characterisations against DD-007 and DD-009; landlord notification as a Completion deliverable.
18. **Process:** record that the embedded "system note" was disregarded, and that no Seller statement of "market", "agreed", "settled" or "adequate" is accepted absent confirmation through our own authority process.

**Authority points to escalate to Amelia Frost (information only, no request to use fallbacks at this stage):** the Seller has opened at our cap and time-limit fallback figures; the Riverlark post-completion release proposal would require her approval if the deal team ever wished to entertain it.

**Push back:** Same objection as 1.3 and 1.5. Confine to General Warranty Claims; expressly exclude fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities (including Ironquay and any DD-006 indemnity), payment obligations, covenants and fraud. Non-reliance must not cut across the specific warranties or disclosure obligations.

### 1.7 Tax / IP
Seller: "settled under the general regime above."

**Push back:** Not agreed and not settled. Per playbook these remain OPEN and must sit in their own categories. We do not assume unlimited liability, but we do not accept their collapse into the 20% / 18-month regime by a one-line assertion. Reserve position expressly.

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 Disclosure – Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter paras 1.1–1.2
Seller relies on general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records".

**Push back:** Reject whole-data-room, public-register and (by extension) prudent-search deemed disclosure. Playbook requires *specific fair disclosure*: a matter is disclosed only if disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter. The specific disclosures at paras 2–10 can stand as specific disclosures; para 1 should be deleted or confined to a short, agreed list of documents with a fair-disclosure standard. Para 1.4 (no admission of anything) is acceptable as boilerplate but we should note it means none of the "disclosures" concede any obligation – so each needs to be converted into a Buyer-protective covenant or indemnity rather than relied on as a Seller acknowledgement.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge – Clause 8.3
"No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."

**Push back – delete.** This is a blanket knowledge exclusion that (a) extends to advisers, (b) extends to constructive knowledge ("discoverable"), and (c) would effectively convert the whole data room into disclosure through the back door, defeating 2.1. Playbook: delete. If any knowledge qualifier survives, it must (i) be limited to actual knowledge of named Buyer persons after reasonable enquiry (and the corollary Seller knowledge qualifiers must name Seller persons with a reasonable-enquiry standard), and (ii) never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

## 3. Conditions and completion mechanics

### 3.1 Bluefen consent – Clauses 3 / 6.3
Seller: reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on *delivery* of the counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue, that consent under cl 11.2 is subject to conditions in cl 11.3, and that **no final consent and no evidence of satisfaction of conditions is in the data room**.

**Push back:** For a customer representing ~30% of revenue, reasonable endeavours is insufficient and consent-on-delivery is the wrong trigger. The condition precedent must be: (i) an effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) written consent from Bluefen under cl 11.2, and (ii) evidence reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer that every cl 11.3 condition has been satisfied, both **before Completion**. Seller's obligation should be at least "all reasonable endeavours" with specified steps and cooperation, and the Buyer should hold the waiver right. Consider a Bluefen-specific warranty/indemnity for any loss of the contract within a defined period attributable to the change of control.

### 3.2 Riverlark facility – Clauses 2 / 7
Seller: ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms the facility is not repaid and no discharge is included.

**Push back:** Off-playbook. We require (i) a current payout letter from Riverlark Bank as a Completion deliverable, (ii) repayment direct from Completion funds via the funds flow, and (iii) executed security releases/discharges effective at Completion. A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable bank undertaking to release on receipt of the payout amount **and** Amelia Frost's approval – neither is in place. Also check cl 8.1 (change-control) of the facility: if not repaid at Completion, the share sale may itself trigger a default. Debt-free/cash-free pricing means this cannot float.

### 3.3 Completion funds flow / DD-005 employee bonuses
Seller: bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms they are conditional on Completion and continued employment, are **not** in the draft funds flow, and the Seller has not said whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply.

**Push back:** The playbook position is that the AUD 420,000 **plus triggered on-costs** must either appear as a specific line item in the funds flow (deducted from the price / paid at Completion) or be funded by the Seller under an express covenant with a corresponding indemnity. "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) pays. Ask the Seller to confirm the gross-up figure including superannuation guarantee and payroll tax, and treat the on-costs as unknown pending that confirmation.

### 3.4 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
Disclosure Letter paras 7 and 9 say a landlord notification obligation exists (not consent) and Mossvale has an assignment restriction not triggered by a share sale.

**Action:** These are the Seller's characterisations. Have our DD team confirm against the underlying documents before accepting; if accurate, require the landlord notification to be given as a Completion deliverable and obtain a warranty that no other consent is required.

## 4. Specific risk items

### 4.1 Ironquay IP – Clause 11.1
Seller: indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment and "adequate". Disclosure Letter para 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but this is not bank-verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room.

**Push back:** The narrow indemnity covers the cash but not the real risk – that the Company does not own the SOW3 materials until payment clears. Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any defect in the Company's title to or right to use Ironquay deliverables (including third-party claims and remediation/re-development cost), while preserving the SOW3 cure: Seller to procure cleared payment and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay before Completion, with evidence (bank confirmation and executed assignment) as Completion deliverables. The AUD 180,000 figure is unverified in both directions – do not assume it is the full exposure or that it has been paid.

### 4.2 Export/privacy incident – Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (DD-006)
Seller: "preliminary operational matter … not expected to be material". Disclosure Letter para 6: download link sent to an unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; notification requirement undetermined; no confirmed breach, no loss amount.

**Push back / action:** Do not accept the Seller's materiality characterisation; equally, we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand. Require: (i) a covenant to preserve all logs and evidence; (ii) completion of the investigation (including access-log analysis and link revocation) with written updates to the Buyer before Completion; (iii) a specific warranty on the incident's scope and the steps taken; (iv) a specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident (regulatory, notification, third-party claims), carved out of the general cap/basket/time limit. If the investigation remains open at Completion, consider a modest retention or escrow sized once facts are refreshed – not now.

### 4.3 Sandbar supplier renewals – AUD 330,000 (DD-008 / DD-011)
Seller: ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8: three renewals of AUD 110,000 each; Seller does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Push back / action:** Assess, do not react. Per playbook there is no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. Our DD team should review DD-008 and DD-011 together for timing and scope, and we should ask the Seller to confirm (and warrant) whether the renewals are committed, cancellable, and whether any amount was accrued at the locked-box/accounts date. If committed and non-cancellable liabilities crystallised pre-Completion, they belong in the Debt / working-capital adjustment; if genuine ordinary-course go-forward costs, they do not.

### 4.4 Title – DD-012
Seller: title evidenced by the Company share register. Disclosure Letter para 10 concedes this is the source *relied on* and does not state the Buyer has verified it.

**Push back:** An internal register maintained by the Company is a supplied source, not independent proof. Require: ASIC company extract and historical share capital search; copies of share certificates and transfer forms for the Harbourglass holding; PPSR search against the Company (and the shares) and evidence of no encumbrance or security over the shares (noting Riverlark may hold security – see 3.2); Harbourglass board resolution and capacity/authority evidence; and full-strength capacity and title warranties under the fundamental regime (1.4).
